# Aseprite import fixtures

The following files come from [Aseprite's official test sprites](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/tree/main/tests/sprites), retrieved on 2026-09-05:

- `1empty3`: empty frames
- `2f-index-3x3`, `4f-index-4x4`: indexed animation
- `abcd`: static indexed work with layers
- `bg-index-3`: background and nonzero transparent index
- `groups2`, `groups3abc`: hidden layers and nested groups
- `link`, `tags3`: linked cels and animation
- `z-order`: cel stacking
- `2x2tilemap2x2tile`: unsupported tilemap error case

These upstream fixtures are distributed under the MIT license in [LICENSE.txt](LICENSE.txt). They are test artwork, not user artwork.

`alpha-offset` and `grayscale` are generated by this project's `create-extra-fixtures.lua`, covering opacity, clipping, and grayscale+alpha.

Each `.rgba` file is the concatenation of full-canvas, row-major RGBA frames rendered by **Aseprite itself**, not the importer. Regenerate with the installed Aseprite CLI:

```sh
aseprite --batch --script-param root="$PWD/tests/fixtures/aseprite" --script tests/fixtures/aseprite/render-reference.lua
```

The test compares every visible channel against those native reference frames. Color channels under fully transparent pixels are normalized because native grayscale and RGBA rendering preserve them differently.
